agents.reasoning: Per-share figures are per CURRENT pre-split share (today's Class A share plus the Class C share it gets in the Jan-2027 dividend; 8-K 2026-10-21); EV is unchanged by the dividend. Evidence, mostly primary: Q3-26 release, 10-Q and call; Q2-26 call; nine prior releases for the guidance record. The core is strong: revenue +26% (impressions +10%, price +14%), Q4 guide $73-76B (+22-27%), and Meta beat the top of its range in 6 of 8 quarters. The debate is cost: FY26 expenses $175-179B (incl. $12.3B legal), capex $135-145B, $454.5B of non-cancelable commitments ($121.4B due 2027), management 'investing aggressively' in 2027, and RL loss ~$15B. Driver build: FY27 revenue $312B (at consensus) from impressions +9% and price +10% plus new AI revenue; FoA margin 51.6% FY25 -> 37.8% FY27 -> 34.5% FY28 as D&A rises with capex that follows the AI capex file ($192B, $236B; above street). FY27 EPS ~$32 (~5% below consensus $33.9). Valuation: SOTP $750 (FoA 16.5x NTM EBIT, RL -$25B), P/E 20x $691, EV/EBITDA 10x $681 -> research target (12m) $715.83, +11% vs $642.62. Scenarios: bear $409 (25%), base $716 (50%), bull $1,019 (25%). Ladder: 75% this scenario mix (within-scenario vol 17-18%) plus 25% a market-anchored lognormal (median $650, sigma 33%, about the stock's 43% realized vol trimmed for non-earnings periods), since price is the best single forecast. That gives a median of ~$697 and P(>= $643) = 0.59. Not driver-linked: the RL venture value (-$25B), the litigation and investment adjustments, and RL revenue. Research limits: the Q3 call transcript was reached at a content_files URL; no option data was used.

agents.reasoning: Per-share figures are per CURRENT pre-split share (today's Class A share plus the Class C share it receives on 2027-01-19); EV is unchanged by the dividend. Industry lane: the rest of the ad chain says demand is still strong but slowing. WARC's Q3-26 outlook has social ad spend +21.3% in 2026 and +14.6% in 2027, total +11.9% then +8.4% [13]; IAB US social +16.5% in 2026 [14]; Google Search +17%, YouTube +13%, Amazon ads +26%, Reddit ads +64%, Pinterest +18%, Snap ads only +9% in Q2-26 [16-20]; eMarketer puts Meta's 2026 ad revenue at ~$242B [30]. Meta's own impressions growth fell from +19% (Q1) to +10% (Q3) while price per ad rose to +14% [6][5][1]; an agency newsletter reports large CPM rises [31] (lead only, low weight). On the cost side the supply chain says Meta's bill keeps rising: CoreWeave $21B through 2032 [21], Nebius $12B from early 2027 [22], DRAM contract prices still rising [23], neocloud rental pricing up >50% YTD (MS proprietary index, used only as direction) [25], $454.5B of non-cancelable commitments and $355.7B of leases not yet commenced [2]. So the driver build has FY2027 revenue +17.7% (impressions +8%, price +9%), 2.4% under consensus, and FoA margin falling to 37.4% as D&A rises to $47B; FY2027 EPS ~$31 vs $33.92 consensus. Capex follows the AI-capex file base ($141B in 2026, $192B in 2027) [24]. Guidance record: five straight quarterly revenue guides at or above the range (median +3.4% vs midpoint), expense guides inside, capex guides overshot in 2024-25. Valuation: SOTP (FoA 16x EV/EBIT, RL separately at -$94B), P/E 19x and EV/EBITDA 10.5x give a research target (12m) of $691 after -$19.9B accrued legal and -$10.5B probability-weighted litigation. Ladder: bear $455 / base $680 / bull $920 at 25/50/25 with 25% within-scenario vol (total ~35% log vol vs 43% realized); the centre (~$670 median) sits between the price and the research target because the price is the better one-year predictor. No option data used. Research limited: Q3-26 peer results (Alphabet, Snap, Pinterest, Reddit) are not out yet; X/Twitter not used; no prediction market found on a Meta event that matters (Kalshi lists only headcount contracts). In-lane sources: 19 of 31.

agents.reasoning: All per-share figures are per CURRENT pre-split share: today's Class A share plus the one Class C share it receives in the dividend payable after the 2027-01-19 charter date; enterprise value is unchanged by it. Evidence: Q3-26 revenue +26% (impressions +10%, price +14%), Q4 guide $73-76B; Meta has finished 2-4% above the revenue guide midpoint in each of the last four quarters, so we sit at the top ($76.1B). FY2026 expenses land at the $177B guide midpoint (incl. $12.3B legal charges). The stock fell ~8% after a beat on the Class C news and capex fears, the third negative print reaction in a row, after a ~25% September rally on the Muse launch; consensus FY2027 EPS is $33.92. Driver build: ads +19% in 2027 and +14% in 2028; FoA margin falls from ~44% ex-charges to 38% and 35.5% because D&A climbs from $28B to ~$71B on capex of $141B/$205B/$252B (AI-file base, with Meta's record of exceeding first capex guides by 16-21% in up-years); 2027 EPS ~$31.7 is ~6% below consensus for that reason. Valuation: 21x NTM P/E (15% below the peer median, mid of META's 2026 range of 18-23x) and a SOTP with FoA at 16x EBIT and RL on its own give a research target (12m) of $725. Base rates: META's own 12-month return s.d. is ~0.42 and its post-drawdown history is very strong, but survivor-biased; Kalshi prices a 20% chance of a 2027 recession and META's price per ad fell 18% y/y in 2022, which sets the bear weight. Prediction markets on META itself (Polymarket via Polyguana) are short-dated and thin, so they carry no weight. Ladder: three lognormals at the engine's bear ($477, 25%, s.d. 0.27) and bull ($939, 25%, s.d. 0.22) and a base shaded from $725 to $705 toward price-plus-drift ($700) because research targets have overshot; median ~$702, mean ~$725, P(above today) 0.60. Not driver-linked: the investments adjustment (+$24.5B) and the stated net debt at horizon. Research was limited by blocked pages (S&P/Visible Alpha previews, Nasdaq), and no option data was used.
